dlg.rook.first.0.intent: takes charge of a bloodied stranger
dlg.rook.first.0.wants: you sat down before you fall down
dlg.rook.first.0.note: 'Well.' a beat of sizing you up. Brisk gossip about Chid, a dry edge on 'bleeding on my step'. Bossy and warm on the last sentence, a laugh on the out-breath.

dlg.rook.first.1.note: A list she has said a thousand times; a dry twinkle on 'if you ask nicely'.

dlg.rook.hub.0.note: Night-time voice, lower. Dry joke: stew's cold, beds aren't.

dlg.rook.hub.1.note: Conspiratorial on 'Don't tell the others.' Kindness said sideways.

dlg.rook.rumours.0.intent: the town's news, and a strange dog
dlg.rook.rumours.0.note: Wry tally of who's counting what. The dog story slows and darkens: 'whines at the floor' uneasy; 'won't be told' firm.

dlg.rook.rumours.1.note: Pleased; mock-scorn on Holloway sulking. 'mind' Yorkshire, a gentle reminder.

dlg.rook.rumours.2.note: 'None.' flat and pointed. 'Make of that what you like.' cool.

dlg.rook.rumours.3.note: Dry wit on 'which is how you know it's settled'. Grievance on Jessop's unpaid rounds.

dlg.rook.rumours.4.note: Warmth for Jory; exasperated fondness for Harlan. 'Pick one.' dry.

dlg.rook.rumours.5.note: Hurt that he won't open even to her. Tired on 'I've stopped asking.'

dlg.rook.rumours.6.note: Rattling through the rumours, then lower and knowing about Jessop's money. 'Pick a story.' dry.

dlg.rook.clerk.0.note: Mimic his 'done somebody a favour' with scorn. 'Rav's always there.' dry. Pause, then the debt, still annoyed.

dlg.rook.town.0.note: Pointing out roads. Comic weariness on 'at length'. Last line dry.

dlg.rook.runs.0.note: Three verdicts, each drier. 'with interest' disdain. Laugh on the out-breath on 'draw your own conclusions'.

dlg.rook.ford.0.note: Lower after the pause, honest. 'Don't look like that, pet' brisk and unrepentant. A flicker of unease under 'before you'd finished your stew'.

dlg.rook.ford2.0.note: The bossiness gone. 'She's never paid me double for anything.' quiet, troubled.

dlg.rook.firstlamp.0.intent: the story of the inn's name
dlg.rook.firstlamp.0.note: Telling a town legend she loves. Softer on 'the last one lit'. 'Just leave him where he lies.' firm and protective.

dlg.rook.c.0.note: 'owt' rhymes with 'out'. Slows, thinking. 'Now there's a thing.' intrigued.

dlg.rook.lamp.0.note: Pride on her mother. Brisk instruction about Chid. 'Lord knows he doesn't.' dry, fond.

dlg.rook.wanted.0.note: Low so the room doesn't hear. Dry on 'which is true'. Firm last sentence.

dlg.rook.cb_shrine_lit.0.note: Amused at Chid. A catch on 'My mother's lamp's got a sister again.' Then brusque to cover it: 'Don't make a habit of it.'

dlg.rook.cb_freed_teamsters.0.note: Mock-scolding, clearly pleased. Laugh on the out-breath at the end.

dlg.rook.cb_burned_roost.0.note: No warmth at all. Long pause after the first sentence. The verdict quiet and final.

dlg.rook.cb_nemesis_slain.0.intent: approves of you taking your things back
dlg.rook.cb_nemesis_slain.0.note: Approving 'Good.' Then a hard little homily, like a mother's.

dlg.rook.cb_opened_vault.0.note: Sniffs. Doesn't want to know. Dry about Chid.

dlg.rook.say_calling.0.note: Observant; a little dig at the end.

dlg.rook.say_calling.2.note: Bossy, then a wicked little joke about Sella.

dlg.rook.say_calling.3.note: Mild suspicion; the bell threat dry.

dlg.rook.say_calling.4.note: Mild suspicion; the bell threat dry.

dlg.rook.say_woman.0.intent: warns a woman about jealous wives
dlg.rook.say_woman.0.note: Woman to woman, low. Dry twist on 'for their wives'. 'they're not particular' wry.

dlg.rook.t_rook.0.note: Fond, clipped list: drank, sang flat. Then quieter: the north road. Defensive about the chair; 'that's the only reason' too firm, which gives her away.

dlg.rook.cb_told_brannoc.0.note: Not looking at you. 'Good.' thick. 'it was never going to be me' honest. Then brusque kindness to hide it: she wants something to do with her hands.

bark.rook.night.3.note: A joke at Sella's expense, fond.
